column3: It directly joins worldly enjoyment's deception to the Day of Resurrection and the final divergent outcome.

Deeds being brought forth on the Day develops the accountability implicit in being presented.

The extraction of a witness from every community develops the public, compulsory character of the final encounter.

God's gathering on the Day makes worldly duration seem momentary and turns people toward recognition of loss.

Wealth and children are worldly adornment, whereas enduring good deeds are better in reward and hope.
Worldly splendor is identified as a test, while the Lord's provision is better and more lasting.

It explicitly says that all will be raised on the Day of Resurrection.
Worldly life is diversion and play, while the Hereafter is the true life for those who know.
Knowing only the outward worldly life is contrasted with heedlessness of the Hereafter.
A brief worldly enjoyment is followed by compulsion toward severe punishment.
The warning against worldly deception and false security before God's promise directly supports the focus's contrast.
The promised day has an appointed time that cannot be delayed or advanced.
Whatever is given is worldly enjoyment, while what is with God is better and more enduring for believers.
Worldly life is play and diversion, and faith prevents the loss that pursuit of it can cause.
Wealth and children are warned against as distractions from God's remembrance, naming a mechanism of worldly absorption.
The Day of Gathering reveals gain and loss, with believers receiving forgiveness and gardens beneath which rivers flow.
Love of the immediate world is directly contrasted with neglect of the Hereafter.
Leaving the Hereafter completes the focus's contrast between present enjoyment and final destination.
Transgression joined to preference for worldly life leads to Hell as the final refuge.
Fearing one's standing before the Lord and restraining desire leads to the Garden, furnishing the positive counterpart.
Preference for worldly life is explicitly corrected by the claim that the Hereafter is better and more lasting.
